title: Catch-22
events_chronological: Yossarian arrives on the island and flies his first missions as a bombardier.
Snowden is hit over Avignon and dies in Yossarian's arms as Yossarian finds the second wound under his flak suit.
Colonel Cathcart raises the number of missions needed to go home, and then raises it again, and again.
Yossarian reports sick with a liver complaint just short of jaundice and stays in hospital as long as the doctors will allow.
Yossarian censors the enlisted men's letters out of boredom and signs them with a borrowed name.
An investigator arrives to look into the forged signatures and finds nothing at all.
Doc Daneeka explains that asking to be grounded for madness is proof of sanity, and therefore no grounds for anything.
Milo Minderbinder builds a syndicate trading across both sides of the front and corners the entire Egyptian cotton crop.
Milo contracts with the enemy to bomb his own squadron for an agreed fee.
A relentlessly cheerful patient drives every other man out of the ward.
Clevinger is tried for an offence nobody can name, and later flies into a cloud and is never seen again.
Doc Daneeka is recorded as dead because his name was on a flight manifest, and no amount of paperwork can bring him back.
Nately falls in love with a prostitute who is asleep every time he calls.
Nately is killed over Spezia, and his prostitute blames Yossarian and tries to knife him wherever he goes.
The military police turn the apartments out, and Yossarian walks back through the city alone past one atrocity after another.
Aarfy rapes and kills a maid and is not arrested, while Yossarian is arrested for being in the city without a pass.
Cathcart and Korn offer Yossarian a bargain: say the squadron is wonderful and go home a hero.
Yossarian refuses the bargain, learns that Orr has rowed all the way to Sweden, and sets off to follow him.
syuzhet_notes: Chapters are named for people rather than for moments, and the same episodes recur out of order with more of the truth each time. The gunner's death in particular is approached again and again and only completed at the end.
fabula_notes: The chronology is recoverable almost entirely from the rising mission count, which the novel repeats constantly. Nothing else fixes it.
